Kuzmyntsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Kuz'myntsi's Jewish community was small even at its peak — about 50 people out of 1,088 residents by 1897 — and suffered a pogrom that killed 6 in 1918. Under Romanian administration as part of the Transnistria Governorate from 1941, a ghetto here absorbed deportees from Bessarabia and Bukovina alongside local Jews; 225 died, and only 128 remained by September 1943. Remarkably, the cemetery itself survived into the early 1980s — a local resident recalled it still holding 5 or 6 tombstones as late as 1983 — before it was finally demolished.
